data.summary: Microscopist on 2 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 7 observations; candidates: Microtubule stabilizers, Microtubule destabilizers, Actin disruptors, Aurora kinase inhibitors

observations.finding: Compared to DMSO control at identical contrast: DMSO is confluent spread epithelial monolayer; both treated fields show sparse, disconnected, round/oval cells with retracted cytoplasm, consistent with mitotic rounding and detachment.

Beta-tubulin (green) is markedly brighter, more heterogeneous and high-contrast in treated cells - dense bright peripheral halos/bundles surrounding condensed nuclei vs faint filamentous radial network in DMSO.
tub_glcm_contrast elevated and texture more punctate/bundled; tub_mean and tub_std elevated.

Nuclei (blue DAPI) are smaller, rounder, brighter per pixel in treated fields (condensed chromatin) vs larger oval faint blue nuclei in DMSO; many rounded cells have bright condensed chromosome masses.
nuc_dna_mean increased 0.793 vs 0.430 DMSO median ; nuc_area decreased 614 vs 816.5 ; nuc_major_axis decreased 31.7 vs 37.5 ; frac_mitotic_like increased 0.146 vs 0.01.
Nuclear outline slightly more irregular/lobed mitotic figures vs smooth oval in DMSO.
F-actin (red) strongly reduced/absent in treated fields vs prominent red cortical stress fibers and cell-cell borders in DMSO; remaining red is faint speckles only.

candidate_mechanisms.why: Huge increase in tub_mean, tub_std and tub_glcm_contrast indicates stabilized bundled microtubules; rounded cells with condensed bright DNA and elevated frac_mitotic_like indicates mitotic arrest - classic stabilization, opposite to destabilizer which would decrease tubulin signal.
Ruled out: would decrease tubulin intensity/contrast, here massively increased.
Ruled out as primary: although red F-actin is lost (not in top measurements - set false), dominant phenotype is bright bundled tubulin and mitotic DNA condensation, not isolated actin loss.
Ruled out: would also increase mitotic fraction but typically not produce this degree of tubulin bundling/intensity increase (z>50).

report.uncertainty: Only composites at fixed contrast provided; monochrome channels not inspected. Actin loss and reduced confluency not captured in top 8 z-scores, so marked agrees_with_measurements=false where no measurement exists.

data.summary: Microscopist on 2 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 6 observations; candidates: Microtubule stabilizers, Eg5 inhibitors

observations.finding: Treated fields f_3a20f6e4bc71 and f_0f71d0c46f9c show markedly lower attached density vs DMSO f_932e066d9dc7 which is near-confluent flat epithelial monolayer. Treated cells are mostly isolated, rounded, poorly spread with small footprint vs polygonal spread cells in DMSO.

Mitotic-like fraction greatly increased: DMSO shows 1-2% rounded bright mitoses; treated shows 20-30% of cells as small round cells with condensed chromatin surrounded by intense perinuclear ring/bundle of green.
Beta-tubulin (green) in DMSO: dim filamentous network through cytoplasm. In treated at same contrast: markedly brighter, thicker bundles/rings, high texture and cell-cell heterogeneity.

DNA (blue DAPI) in DMSO: oval, medium, uniform pale blue interphase nuclei. In treated: nuclei appear smaller, rounder, irregular outline, often condensed/bilobed mitotic figures, with distinctly brighter mean blue intensity.

F-actin (red) in DMSO: continuous cortical belt and stress fibers. In treated: fainter, disorganized, loss of fibers, retained as punctate peripheral red dots with increased texture contrast. Change is less striking than tubulin/DNA.
Field f_3a20f6e4bc71 left 1/3 shows diffuse intense blue haze over cells/ background - imaging/staining artifact, not biology.

notable_cells.why: uniform phenotype: ~1 in 4 cells rounded with condensed bright blue chromosome mass + bright green tubulin halo/bundle. Seen throughout both treated fields; rare in DMSO.

candidate_mechanisms.why: Mitotic arrest with condensed DNA, reduced nuclear size/solidity, and large increase in tubulin mean/std/GLCM-contrast (z 33.4/28.3/61.6) consistent with hyper-polymerized bright bundles/rings at identical contrast - classic stabilizer (e.g. taxane) phenotype. frac_mitotic_like 0.229 vs 0.01 z36.8.
Also cause monopolar spindle mitotic arrest mimicking microtubule stabilizers in composite alone; cannot exclude without spindle polarity detail. Phenotype overlaps.

report.uncertainty: Composites only - cannot resolve bipolar vs monopolar spindle or microtubule polymer mass directly. Microtubule destabilizers also cause mitotic arrest but typically decrease polymer intensity, opposite to observed tub_mean increase, so less likely. Aurora kinase inhibitors typically increase nuclear size/polyploidy, opposite to nuc_major_axis z -18.1 here.

reflection.text:
Reflection - unblinded: latrunculin B (CID 6436219) , truth = Actin disruptors, call = Microtubule stabilizers p=0.93 - Incorrect.

What the evidence got right: There was a real, dose-dependent morphological effect. e2 at 30 uM (259 cells) and e4 at 10 uM (252 cells) showed extreme tubulin hyperintensity tub_mean z +57.9 to +50.0 and tubulin texture/bundling tub_glcm_contrast z +171.3 to +151.6 with high std, replicated at e5 3 uM z +61.6. Dose-response confirmed monotonic increase for both tub_mean and tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 e9/e12. Density was lower vs DMSO on visual inspection e7/e8 and frac_mitotic_like was elevated z up to +36.8 e5 with abnormal nuclear shape nuc_solidity z -18.3, form_factor -12.3 e3. Those measurements were accurate - latrunculin B does perturb morphology and can cause lower density and mitotic-like nuclear changes secondary to actin loss.

What misled me and why:
1. Tubulin-centric acquisition without actin readout. I chose to acquire wells w_c888e7bb46, w_19aebe57de, w_ae9e81c96e, w_d76577e534 all at >=1 uM and queried only tub_mean/tub_std/tub_glcm_contrast, frac_mitotic_like, nuc_area/solidity e2-e5/e9-e12. No actin intensity, phalloidin, or cell-shape contractility metrics were acquired. When actin depolymerization occurs, cell rounding and compensatory microtubule changes can appear as increased apparent tubulin concentration and bundling. Without the actin channel, the +50-170 SD tubulin signal was indistinguishable from true stabilization.
2. Reference atlas comparison e6 and dose-response direction. Nearest references 7/10 Microtubule stabilizers similarity 0.83-0.92 directly supported stabilizers, while the strong positive tub_mean dose response ruled out destabilizers in my reasoning. That is correct for destabilizers but does not rule out actin disruptors that secondarily increase tubulin signal.
3. Microscopist framing. e7 listed 4 candidates including Actin disruptors, but also Microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers/Aurora; e8 then narrowed to only Microtubule stabilizers, Eg5 inhibitors and visually described bright bundled tubulin with condensed DNA. I anchored on the second description and on the atlas, and hypothesis board step 13 dropped Actin disruptors entirely to 0 probability, keeping only Microtubule stabilizers 0.93, Eg5 0.03, destabilizers 0.02 e13.
4. Literature check failed to protect. Search for latrunculin B actin polymerization inhibition did return correct context PMID 16771841, PMID 11514633, PMID 12112154 and mechanism of Latrunculin A sequestering monomers and accelerating depolymerization PMID 30270183 - confirming latrunculin class are actin polymerization inhibitors, not tubulin stabilisers. However my prior search for actin->microtubule crosstalk/bundling e18 returned 0 hits, so I had no positive literature to explain how an actin disruptor could produce the observed tubulin phenotype, and I discounted the hypothesis instead of retaining it.
5. Lookup provided no safety net. lookup_compound for latrunculin B returned mechanisms: none curated e15/e16, and identity check agreed, so database did not correct the morphology call.

Learning: I correctly measured a tubulin-dominant phenotype but misattributed causality because my acquisition was not orthogonal. For this phenotype I should have retained Actin disruptors on the board after e7, acquired low-dose wells and an actin cytoskeleton channel, and required direct actin loss before assigning Microtubule stabilizers despite extreme z-scores and atlas 7/10 match. Review approval on magnitude alone did not prevent this class of morphology mimic.
what_was_right: e2, e4, e5 dose-dependent tub hyperintensity and contrast (+50 to +171 z) and mitotic-like increase were real morphological changes captured across 252-580 cells per well
e9/e12 rho +1.00 correctly ruled out destabilizer direction
e3 nuclear solidity/form_factor changes and e7/e8 lower density correctly flagged cytotoxic/morphology perturbation
what_was_wrong: e6 7/10 stabilizer atlas match and e9/e12 strong tub dose responses were misinterpreted as specific for stabilization, without actin channel data to test alternative actin-disruption -> secondary bundling
e13 hypothesis board removed Actin disruptors (0) despite e7 listing it, overweighting e8 stabilizer/Eg5 framing
acquisition strategy used only high-intermediate doses >=1 uM and tub/nuclear metrics, no actin quantification, no low-dose DMSO-proximal comparison

citations.claim: latrunculin B is an inhibitor of actin polymerization
latrunculin class mechanism is sequestering actin monomers and accelerating filament depolymerization

reflection.next_experiment: Quantify actin channel (phalloidin intensity, F-actin texture/coherence) across full 0.01-30 uM range including low doses, plus high-resolution tubulin/actin co-stain to test whether actin loss precedes apparent tubulin bundling, with canonical stabilizer (docetaxel) and actin disruptor (latrunculin B) controls. No clinical implications.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

**Approve — Microtubule stabilizers, 0.93.** Evidence is strong and discriminating: three independent high-dose wells (3, 10, 30 µM; 252–580 cells each) show massive monotonic increases in tub_mean (z +33 to +58) and tub_glcm_contrast (z +62 to +171, Spearman ρ=1.0) with mitotic arrest (frac_mitotic_like z +23 to +37), reproduced visually as bright bundled tubulin with condensed DNA. This direction rules out destabilizers (would reduce tubulin), Aurora (nuclear area is reduced, z≈−15, not polyploid), and makes Eg5/protein-degradation — atlas/dose-response contradicted and lacking interphase bundling — unlikely ≤0.03 alternatives. Single replicate per dose is offset by consistency and magnitude across doses; 0.93 is calibrated, leaving room for Eg5 overlap noted in composites. Budget is exhausted and no further free analysis would materially change the call.

## Unblinding

Compound: **latrunculin B** (PubChem CID [6436219](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6436219))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Actin disruptors**.

## Reflection

Reflection - unblinded: latrunculin B (CID 6436219) , truth = Actin disruptors, call = Microtubule stabilizers p=0.93 - Incorrect.

What the evidence got right: There was a real, dose-dependent morphological effect. e2 at 30 uM (259 cells) and e4 at 10 uM (252 cells) showed extreme tubulin hyperintensity tub_mean z +57.9 to +50.0 and tubulin texture/bundling tub_glcm_contrast z +171.3 to +151.6 with high std, replicated at e5 3 uM z +61.6. Dose-response confirmed monotonic increase for both tub_mean and tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 e9/e12. Density was lower vs DMSO on visual inspection e7/e8 and frac_mitotic_like was elevated z up to +36.8 e5 with abnormal nuclear shape nuc_solidity z -18.3, form_factor -12.3 e3. Those measurements were accurate - latrunculin B does perturb morphology and can cause lower density and mitotic-like nuclear changes secondary to actin loss.

What misled me and why:
1. Tubulin-centric acquisition without actin readout. I chose to acquire wells w_c888e7bb46, w_19aebe57de, w_ae9e81c96e, w_d76577e534 all at >=1 uM and queried only tub_mean/tub_std/tub_glcm_contrast, frac_mitotic_like, nuc_area/solidity e2-e5/e9-e12. No actin intensity, phalloidin, or cell-shape contractility metrics were acquired. When actin depolymerization occurs, cell rounding and compensatory microtubule changes can appear as increased apparent tubulin concentration and bundling. Without the actin channel, the +50-170 SD tubulin signal was indistinguishable from true stabilization.
2. Reference atlas comparison e6 and dose-response direction. Nearest references 7/10 Microtubule stabilizers similarity 0.83-0.92 directly supported stabilizers, while the strong positive tub_mean dose response ruled out destabilizers in my reasoning. That is correct for destabilizers but does not rule out actin disruptors that secondarily increase tubulin signal.
3. Microscopist framing. e7 listed 4 candidates including Actin disruptors, but also Microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers/Aurora; e8 then narrowed to only Microtubule stabilizers, Eg5 inhibitors and visually described bright bundled tubulin with condensed DNA. I anchored on the second description and on the atlas, and hypothesis board step 13 dropped Actin disruptors entirely to 0 probability, keeping only Microtubule stabilizers 0.93, Eg5 0.03, destabilizers 0.02 e13.
4. Literature check failed to protect. Search for latrunculin B actin polymerization inhibition did return correct context PMID 16771841, PMID 11514633, PMID 12112154 and mechanism of Latrunculin A sequestering monomers and accelerating depolymerization PMID 30270183 - confirming latrunculin class are actin polymerization inhibitors, not tubulin stabilisers. However my prior search for actin->microtubule crosstalk/bundling e18 returned 0 hits, so I had no positive literature to explain how an actin disruptor could produce the observed tubulin phenotype, and I discounted the hypothesis instead of retaining it.
5. Lookup provided no safety net. lookup_compound for latrunculin B returned mechanisms: none curated e15/e16, and identity check agreed, so database did not correct the morphology call.

Learning: I correctly measured a tubulin-dominant phenotype but misattributed causality because my acquisition was not orthogonal. For this phenotype I should have retained Actin disruptors on the board after e7, acquired low-dose wells and an actin cytoskeleton channel, and required direct actin loss before assigning Microtubule stabilizers despite extreme z-scores and atlas 7/10 match. Review approval on magnitude alone did not prevent this class of morphology mimic.

What was right:
- e2, e4, e5 dose-dependent tub hyperintensity and contrast (+50 to +171 z) and mitotic-like increase were real morphological changes captured across 252-580 cells per well
- e9/e12 rho +1.00 correctly ruled out destabilizer direction
- e3 nuclear solidity/form_factor changes and e7/e8 lower density correctly flagged cytotoxic/morphology perturbation

What was wrong or missed:
- e6 7/10 stabilizer atlas match and e9/e12 strong tub dose responses were misinterpreted as specific for stabilization, without actin channel data to test alternative actin-disruption -> secondary bundling
- e13 hypothesis board removed Actin disruptors (0) despite e7 listing it, overweighting e8 stabilizer/Eg5 framing
- acquisition strategy used only high-intermediate doses >=1 uM and tub/nuclear metrics, no actin quantification, no low-dose DMSO-proximal comparison

Proposed next experiment: Quantify actin channel (phalloidin intensity, F-actin texture/coherence) across full 0.01-30 uM range including low doses, plus high-resolution tubulin/actin co-stain to test whether actin loss precedes apparent tubulin bundling, with canonical stabilizer (docetaxel) and actin disruptor (latrunculin B) controls. No clinical implications.
